physics_goals.quote: The Magnetic Calorimeter detector was used to test the Quantumchromodynamic theory of the strong nuclear force, and to measure the lifetime of the B meson.
physics_goals.value: Test quantum chromodynamics, measure electroweak effects and measure the lifetime of the B meson

summary.plain: A detector at SLAC's PEP ring that captured all the energy of electron-positron collisions in a large magnetised calorimeter. It tested quantum chromodynamics, measured electroweak effects in muon pairs and measured the lifetime of the B meson. It ran from about 1980 to 1986.
summary.technical: MAC (MAgnetic Calorimeter) at PEP: large solid-angle electromagnetic/hadronic calorimeter with magnetised iron for muon momentum, magnetic charged-particle tracking (5.7 kG solenoid) and scintillator triggering; 29 GeV e⁺e⁻; 40 pb⁻¹ by May 1983; approved 1977, completed running 1986. Collaboration: Colorado, Frascati, Houston, Northeastern, SLAC/Stanford, Utah, Wisconsin (with LBL).
